verdict.rationale: Adyen's docs describe webhooks that send you a message with the final outcome of asynchronous processes, so you don't have to poll an API. That covers the core push-notification mechanism. The evidence does not list the specific lifecycle event types (authorized, captured, refunded, disputed), how endpoints are registered, or how this applies to in-person/terminal transactions. Missing for 10: documented event types for authorization, capture, refund and dispute; documented webhook endpoint registration; POS-specific webhook coverage; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to payment lifecycle events (authorized, captured, refunded, disputed) via webhooks to drive downstream automations

citations.quote: Webhooks solve this by sending you a message with the final outcome as soon as it is available.
With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
